welcome.body: Your child's best friend for emotional skills. I offer gentle stories that support emotional skills and safe development.
welcome.footer: All content is age-appropriate and designed together with education professionals.

aiConsent.title: Use of AI for Your Child's Content
aiConsent.body: Nuppu uses AI to generate age-appropriate and safe content for your child, such as stories and emotional exercises. The AI may use your child's first name and age group to personalize the content.
aiConsent.checkbox: I consent to the use of AI for personalizing my child's content

aiInfo.title: How AI Is Used in the Nuppu App
bullets: AI is used in a limited way to create stories and emotional or social skills content.
Children cannot chat freely with the AI.
The AI may use the child's first name and age group for personalization.
Data is not used for profiling or training AI models.
You can change or withdraw your consent at any time in Settings.
aiInfo.calloutBody: All content is checked before your child sees it. Data is processed in the EU.

nuppu.name: Nuppu
nuppu.intro: Nuppu is a gentle bunny who walks alongside your child through every feeling. Nuppu can name emotions and notices even the small things. Nuppu never says a feeling is wrong — instead, Nuppu helps you understand where it came from and where it can go.

muru.name: Muru
muru.skills: Security, calming down, coping with disappointment
muru.intro: Muru is calm, gentle, and always ready to listen. Muru reminds us that every feeling is allowed. Around Muru, it's okay to be quiet, sad, or tired — exactly as you are!

hippu.name: Hippu
hippu.skills: Expressing one's own will, boundaries, courage
hippu.intro: Hippu is a curious, independent cat who loves trying new things. Hippu thinks a lot: what do I want, how do I feel, and do I dare say it out loud. Hippu teaches that your own boundaries matter, and that they're allowed to change.

lumo.name: Lumo
lumo.intro: Lumo is a clever, observant fox who helps you look at situations from many angles. Lumo doesn't give ready-made answers — Lumo asks good questions instead. From Lumo you learn that mistakes are part of learning, and that even hard feelings can teach us something.

nupun-kiukkupilvi.title: Nuppu's Anger Cloud
nupun-kiukkupilvi.description: Nuppu doesn't want to stop playing and a big anger comes rushing in — until Mom helps Nuppu find a way to let it float away.
pagesBig:
It was evening in the Pastel Forest. A few pale lavender clouds drifted across the sky, and a thin strip of peach-coloured sun still peeked out from behind the treetops. The forest animals were getting ready for bed.

At Nuppu the bunny's home, it was bedtime routine too.

Nuppu sat on the floor, building a tower out of blocks.

Nuppu: “Now it's time to gather the blocks and go brush your teeth.”

Nuppu: “But I'm still building!”

He placed a yellow block on top of the tower.

Mom: “The tower can wait. You can keep building it tomorrow.”

Nuppu looked at his tower. He didn't want to stop. Not at all.

Nuppu: “I'm not going to brush my teeth!”

Mom reached her hand toward the blocks on the floor.

Then something happened inside Nuppu. His ears began to feel hot. His teeth pressed tightly together and his paws clenched into fists.

And suddenly—

Nuppu: “I DON'T WANT TO GO TO SLEEP!”
He kicked the block tower. Blocks flew across the floor. Nuppu stared at them. His heart was pounding fast.

Mom sat down close to Nuppu.

Mom: “It seems like you have some really big anger right now.”

Nuppu: “YES I DO!”
Mom: “Anger is allowed to come. But blocks may not be kicked. Let's think together about how we could help the anger get smaller.”

Nuppu didn't say anything. He noticed his clenched paws, his hot ears, and his heavy eyelids.

Nuppu yawned.

Nuppu: “I'm tired.”

Mom: “I think you might be. Sometimes, when we're tired, even a small annoyance can feel enormous.”

Nuppu looked at the blocks scattered on the floor. The anger was still in his body. But now Nuppu knew what the feeling was.

Nuppu: “How do you make anger smaller?”

Mom thought for a moment.

Mom: “Would you like to go to your calm-down spot together for a little while?”

Nuppu nodded. Next to his window, he had his own little calm-down spot that he had made together with his mom. Nuppu tucked his favourite stuffed toy under his arm and sat down with Mom on the soft cushions of the calm-down spot.

Mom: “Look at those clouds. What if we imagined that big cloud over there is your anger?”

It was a windy evening, and the clouds were moving fast.

Mom: “When the cloud disappears from view, the anger drifts away with it, too.”

Nuppu focused on watching the cloud, and saw it carry his anger further and further away. At last, the cloud disappeared from sight.

Nuppu's paws weren't clenched quite so tightly into fists anymore. The heat in his ears had faded.

Nuppu: “The anger is still a little bit here.”

Mom: “A few crumbs of anger might still be left — and it doesn't have to disappear all at once, either.”

Nuppu looked at the blocks scattered across the floor.

Nuppu: “I kicked the tower over. That wasn't a nice thing to do.”

Mom: “No, it wasn't. But you can think about what you could do now, now that the anger has eased a little.”

Nuppu picked up one block from the floor. Then another.

Nuppu: “I could pick these up.”

Mom helped Nuppu. Together they put the blocks into the basket.

Nuppu: “Tomorrow I'll build the tower again.”

Mom: “That sounds like a good plan.”
Then Nuppu brushed his teeth and climbed under his soft blanket. Outside, the Pastel Forest was already completely quiet. Nuppu rested his head on the pillow.

Nuppu: “Mom?”

Mom: “Yes?”

Nuppu: “If I get angry again tomorrow, can we choose an anger cloud together again?”

Mom: “Of course.”

Nuppu thought for a moment about the cloud that had carried his anger away. The anger had arrived big and hot. Then Nuppu had noticed it. He had listened to his body and calmed down together with his mom. And little by little, the anger had grown smaller.

Moonlight from the Pastel Forest peeked in through the window.

Nuppu yawned once more and closed his eyes. And before Mom could even say goodnight, the little bunny was already fast asleep.
pagesLittle: Nuppu was building a tower out of blocks.
Mom said it was time to go to sleep.
Nuppu got very angry and kicked the tower down.
Mom sat close. “You have big anger,” Mom said.
They went to the calm-down spot together.
They imagined the anger was a cloud floating away.
Nuppu calmed down and picked up the blocks with Mom.
Then Nuppu went to bed and fell asleep.
nupun-kiukkupilvi.microSupportSkill: Noticing anger in the body and finding a way to calm down
microSupportActions: Name the feeling instead of only the behaviour: “You seem to have big anger right now.”
Let the feeling exist before problem-solving — anger is allowed, hurting things is not.
Try a shared calm-down spot at home, with something soft and familiar nearby.
Use an image together, like a cloud carrying the feeling away, to make it easier to picture the anger easing.
nupun-kiukkupilvi.conversationStarter: Do you remember Nuppu's anger cloud? What could your own calm-down spot look like?

nupun-suuri-ilo.title: Nuppu's Big Joy
nupun-suuri-ilo.description: Nuppu is bursting with joy about spring festival day — until excitement rushes them ahead of their friends. Leea the owl teaches Nuppu three steps to calm a big feeling.
nupun-suuri-ilo.emotionalSkill: Noticing big excitement and calming the body
pagesBig:
The Pastel Forest was a calm and beautiful place.

The trees looked as if they'd been painted in watercolours – pale pink, minty green, and sky blue. A little rabbit named Nuppu lived in the forest. Nuppu was curious and got excited easily.

One spring morning, Nuppu woke up even before sunrise.

Nuppu: – Today is the spring festival!

Something bubbled inside Nuppu.

A warm fizzy feeling filled his chest.

His paws moved almost on their own.

Nuppu: – I have such huge joy.

Maybe the biggest joy ever!

Nuppu bounced out of his burrow. On the path, he met Salli the hedgehog.

Nuppu: – GOOD MORNING, Salli!

Nuppu shouted so loudly that the birds flew up in fright.

Salli: – Good morning… You're certainly in a hurry.
Nuppu didn't stop. Joy pushed him forward like an invisible wind. The journey continued on toward the spring festival.

At the spring festival, they were playing a running game. Everyone lined up and waited for the starting signal.

Narrator: – Get ready… on your marks…

Nuppu's heart was pounding. He already wanted to run.

Before the starting signal sounded, Nuppu shot off down the path.

Lumo: – Hey! Wait! We weren't ready yet!

Nuppu stopped.

Suddenly, his stomach felt strange. The joy wasn't light anymore. It felt heavy, and a little embarrassing.

Nuppu: – I just got too excited.

Nuppu said quietly, looking at the ground.

Wise Leea the owl had been watching the whole thing. She flew down beside Nuppu.

Leea: – Joy is an important and wonderful feeling.

Leea: – But sometimes a feeling grows so big that we act too quickly.

Nuppu: – I didn't mean to be unfair.

Nuppu: – How can I calm down?

Leea nodded.

Leea: – By practising. Let's do three things.

Leea taught Nuppu three steps for calming down.

Leea: – First of all: stop.

Leea: – Don't do anything for a moment.

Leea: – Next: feel your body.

Leea: – Press your paws to the ground and feel the earth beneath them. Where does the joy feel strongest? In your chest? Your tummy? Your legs?

Leea: – Lastly: breathe.

Leea: – Slowly in…

Leea: – and calmly out.

Leea: – Then say to yourself, in your mind: “I am really happy.”

Nuppu followed Leea the owl's instructions.

He breathed in…

and out.

Little by little, the fizzy joy turned soft and warm.

It no longer bounced around everywhere. It no longer pushed Nuppu forward. The joy stayed with him – but calmly now.

Nuppu: – I'm still happy.

Nuppu: – But I'm calm too.

Nuppu went back to the others.

Nuppu: – I'm sorry I ran off too soon. I got so excited that I couldn't wait. Can we play again?

Lumo the fox smiled.

Lumo: – Let's play. All together this time.

This time, Nuppu waited for the starting signal.

He felt the fizzy joy, but he breathed, and kept it just the right size.

After the race, Nuppu sat with his friends for a snack break.

Nuppu: – Today I learned that even joy sometimes needs a little calming down.

Nuppu: – A feeling is allowed to be big, but I can still stop and think.

Leea the owl nodded, pleased.

Leea: – Even good feelings can sometimes grow too big. It's important that we learn to calm down, so that we know how to act wisely.

Spring in the Pastel Forest carried on.

Joy was still there –

not too big,

not too small,

but carried wisely.
pagesLittle: Today is the spring festival! Nuppu felt so happy.
The joy was so big that Nuppu ran off too soon and didn't wait for friends.
The friends were surprised. Nuppu felt a little embarrassed.
Leea the owl taught Nuppu three steps: stop, feel your body, breathe.
Nuppu breathed slowly, and the joy became soft.
Nuppu said sorry and played again with the friends.
This time, Nuppu knew how to wait for their turn.
nupun-suuri-ilo.microSupportSkill: Helping an excited child pause before acting
microSupportActions: Name the good feeling too, not just the tricky ones: “You have such big joy right now!”
Teach the three steps together: stop, feel your body, breathe.
Practise waiting for a starting signal in games, so pausing becomes familiar.
Praise noticing and returning to apologise, not just “getting it right” the first time.
nupun-suuri-ilo.conversationStarter: Do you remember how Nuppu learned to breathe and wait? What happens in your body when you're really excited?

pastellimetsan-taitopaiva.title: The Pastel Forest Skill Day
pastellimetsan-taitopaiva.description: On Skill Day, Nuppu watches Muru, Hippu and Lumo show off their talents and starts to feel small — until a little bird in trouble helps Nuppu discover a strength of their own.
pastellimetsan-taitopaiva.emotionalSkill: Self-worth and not comparing yourself to others
pagesBig:
In the Pastel Forest, the sky was pale blue today. The leaves on the trees swayed quietly in the wind.

The door of a little burrow opened. Nuppu the bunny peeked out.

Nuppu: “Today is Pastel Forest Skill Day!”

Once a year, the forest friends gathered at the big flower meadow to show off the things they could do.

Nuppu bounced along the path. He soon met Muru the bear, standing beside a big rock.

Muru: “Watch this!”

He gripped the rock with his paws.

Muru: “Onnnne… two… three!”

Muru lifted the rock into the air.

Nuppu: “Wow! You're so strong!”

Nuppu looked at his own small paws. I can't lift a rock that big, he thought. Nuppu continued on his way, but now his hops were a little smaller.

Around a bend in the path sat Hippu the cat. Hippu had lined up three pinecones on the ground. Suddenly, she leapt. Hippu flew over all three pinecones and landed softly on her paws.

Hippu: “Ta-da!”

Nuppu: “Wow! You're so skilled at jumping!”

Nuppu tried it himself. He took a run-up. One, two, three… JUMP! THUMP. Nuppu hit the second pinecone and tumbled into the soft moss. Hippu helped him up.

Hippu: “It's okay, Nuppu. I've practised this so many times too.”

But Nuppu looked at his toes. I can't jump like Hippu can, he thought.

Nuppu continued on his way. His hops were even smaller now.

When Nuppu arrived at the flower meadow, Lumo the fox was already there. Lots of forest animals had gathered around Lumo.

Lumo: “Look!”

He had built a big, beautiful star out of twigs, leaves, and flowers. Everyone clapped. Nuppu clapped too. Then his ears drooped down. Muru was strong. Hippu was agile. Lumo came up with clever things.

Nuppu: “What about me?”

Nuppu whispered, and crept away to hide behind a big daisy.

After a little while, Muru, Hippu, and Lumo found him.

Muru: “Nuppu, why are you here all alone?”

Nuppu was quiet for a moment.

Nuppu: “I feel like I'm not good at anything.”

The friends sat down beside him. No one rushed to answer. The wind swayed the daisies.

At last, Lumo asked:

Lumo: “How do you feel right now?”

Nuppu: “Sad.”

Then he thought a little more.

Nuppu: “And… pathetically small.”

Hippu: “Sometimes I feel that way too, when I compare myself to others.”

Muru: “Me too. Even though I'm strong, I can't climb a tree as fast as Hippu.”

Hippu: “And I couldn't carry a rock even two steps!”

Nuppu looked up.

Nuppu: “Really? You couldn't?”

Hippu: “Not at all.”
Lumo: “We don't need to be good at the same things to be important.”

Nuppu thought about what his friends had said. Just then, a small sound came from a nearby bush. “Peep… peep…” The friends turned to look. A little baby bird was huddled on the ground. It had fallen from a low branch and was too scared to move.

Muru approached it. The baby bird backed away. Hippu tried to get closer, but the baby bird trembled.

Then Nuppu sat down a little distance from the chick. Nuppu didn't try to pick the bird up. He didn't try to make it move. He just sat there.

Nuppu: “You must be scared.”

Nuppu: “You can stay right there, quite calmly. I can wait here with you.”

Nuppu breathed slowly. In. And out. Soon, the baby bird began to calm down too. It carefully took one small step. Then another. At last, it scurried over to sit beside Nuppu.

The friends watched quietly.

Muru: “Nuppu, you noticed what the little bird needed.”

Hippu: “And you knew how to be patient.”

Lumo: “And gentle.”

Nuppu blinked. He had never thought that those things could be skills too.

Later, the baby bird's mother found her chick and flew down to it. Nuppu went back to the flower meadow with his friends. There, everyone got to make a little star and write or draw their own strength on it.

Muru drew strong paws, and Hippu drew a big leap. Lumo drew a little lightbulb, because he loved coming up with new ideas. Nuppu thought for a while. Then he drew a big heart on his star.

Nuppu: “My strength is that I can notice other people's feelings.”

He thought for one more moment.

Nuppu: “And I am a good Nuppu.”

Lumo: “Exactly right.”

Nuppu smiled. He understood something important. He didn't need to be like Muru. He didn't need to be like Hippu. And he didn't need to be like Lumo. He got to be Nuppu. Nuppu, who was practising some things. Nuppu, who already knew how to do many things. Nuppu, who sometimes succeeded and sometimes didn't. And Nuppu was always just as valuable, no matter what.
On the way home, Nuppu bounced along the path. This time, he wasn't thinking about whether he jumped as high as Hippu. He bounced exactly the way Nuppu bounces, and it felt really good.

As evening fell over the Pastel Forest, Nuppu looked up at the sky. Many stars were shining up there. Some were bright, some were small. Some could only just barely be seen. But not one single star was trying to shine the same way as another.

Nuppu: “I don't have to be the best to be important.”

Nuppu: “I am valuable, because I am me.”
High above the Pastel Forest, one little star seemed to twinkle right back at him.
pagesLittle: On Skill Day, the friends showed what they could do.
Muru was strong, Hippu could jump far, and Lumo made clever things.
Nuppu didn't know what they were good at, and went to hide.
The friends found Nuppu and listened to how they felt.
Then a little bird needed help. Nuppu sat calmly beside it.
Nuppu was patient and gentle. That was their very own skill!
Nuppu understood: you don't have to be the best to be important.
pastellimetsan-taitopaiva.microSupportSkill: Helping a child value their own strengths without comparing
microSupportActions: Notice out loud when your child shows patience or kindness, not only visible skills like speed or strength.
Avoid ranking children's abilities against each other, even lightly or as a joke.
Ask “what did you enjoy trying?” instead of “who was best?” after group activities.
Remind them that everyone has different strengths, and that is what makes a group work well together.
pastellimetsan-taitopaiva.conversationStarter: Do you remember what Nuppu turned out to be really good at? What is something you are good at that isn't about being fastest or strongest?
